findings.premise: standaloneStoryContext in src/workflow/runners/design-story/standalone.ts hardcodes acceptanceCriteria to an empty array at line 57 and returns an empty constraints array at line 71, so both values are absent by construction rather than by a failed lookup.
findings.evidence: Confirmed verbatim. Both read anchors resolve: standalone.ts:57 returns `acceptanceCriteria: [],` and :71 returns `return { flavor, constraints: [], story, hldSlice };`. The `acceptanceCriteria: []` pattern has exactly ONE non-test source hit, that line. `constraints: []` has two non-test hits, the second being a prompt template in src/prompts rather than code, so the code-side origin is also single.
findings.action: none - both hardcoded stubs confirmed at the cited lines

findings.premise: The standalone.ts module imports ONLY types, so standaloneStoryContext is structurally incapable of reading an artifact: it never opens the artifact store and therefore cannot consult the approved ISSUE or a brainstorm SpecArtifact even in principle.
findings.evidence: Confirmed decisively, and it is the load-bearing premise of the whole record. The probe's read of standalone.ts:20 resolves, and a direct inspection settles the negative claim the probe's own filter could not: the file is 72 lines long, contains exactly TWO import statements, and both are `import type` (DefineConstraint/DefineFlavor/DefineStory, and HldContextSlice). A scan for readFileSync, existsSync, readArtifact, artifactJsonPath and readdirSync returns ZERO hits in the file. So standaloneStoryContext genuinely cannot read an artifact even in principle.
findings.action: none - the structural-incapability claim holds on direct inspection, which is stronger evidence than the grep could give

proposedFix.rationale: No edit needed. Recording that the probe's whole-tree grep for filesystem calls was not scoped to this file and so neither confirmed nor refuted the claim; the file-scoped check is what settles it.

findings.premise: The hardcoded empty acceptanceCriteria at standalone.ts:57 is the ONLY place in the non-test source tree that assigns an empty acceptanceCriteria list, so there is a single origin for the defect rather than several.
findings.evidence: Confirmed under two independent patterns. Both `acceptanceCriteria: \[\]` and the whitespace-tolerant `acceptanceCriteria:\s*\[\s*\]` return exactly one non-test source hit, standalone.ts:57. So the defect has a single origin and the fix has a single place to land rather than several.
findings.action: none - single origin confirmed, which is what makes this a bugfix rather than a sweep

findings.premise: The standalone story context is consumed at exactly two non-test call sites — orchestrator.ts:1916-1917 for the HLD context slice and runners/design-story/index.ts:93-94 for the whole context — and both receive the stub unchanged.
findings.evidence: Confirmed. `standaloneStoryContext(` returns three non-test hits: the declaration at standalone.ts:43 plus exactly two call sites, orchestrator.ts:1917 and runners/design-story/index.ts:94. `isStandaloneParams(` mirrors this with its declaration at :31 plus orchestrator.ts:1916 and index.ts:93. Both read anchors resolve. The consuming surface is therefore two sites, as claimed.
findings.action: none - exactly two consumers, so the blast radius of a signature change is small

findings.premise: DefineStory declares acceptanceCriteria as a REQUIRED array field at src/workflow/artifacts/define.ts:68, so an empty list is schema-valid and passes validation silently rather than being rejected.
findings.evidence: Confirmed. `export interface DefineStory` resolves uniquely at define.ts:64 and `readonly acceptanceCriteria:` at :68, which the read confirms as `readonly acceptanceCriteria:        readonly DefineAcceptanceCriterion[];` — a required field with an array type and no minimum length. An empty array therefore satisfies the type, which is precisely why the pipeline produces one silently.
findings.action: none - the schema permits the empty list, which is why nothing errors and why a gate change is one of the open design questions

findings.premise: The Story's title and userValue both default to the same focus string when triage supplies no storyTitle or storySpec, so they come out identical verbatim — a second symptom of the same stub.
findings.evidence: Confirmed. Both reads resolve: standalone.ts:48 is `const title = strParam(params, 'storyTitle') ?? focus;` and :49 is `const spec = strParam(params, 'storySpec') ?? focus;`, each falling back to the same focus string. This is visible in the live artifact for the folder-fork Story, whose title and userValue are identical verbatim.
findings.action: none - the secondary symptom is real and traced to the same stub

findings.premise: The census the whole record rests on: 55 of 55 standalone LLDs supplied their own acceptance criteria, 163 stories across 31 DEF artifacts have none empty, 141 epic-parented LLDs needed none, and 0 of 21 ISSUE artifacts carry a story list — a 100% failure rate on the standalone route and 0% on the epic route.
findings.evidence: NOT probe-verifiable, and said plainly rather than scored as a confirmation. The two patterns returned 50-hit saturated results with effectively nothing resolving under non-test source, because the census counts values inside artifact JSON under .insrc/artifacts rather than anything in the source tree. The figures were computed by enumerating that store directly: 55 of 55 standalone LLDs supplied their own criteria, 163 stories across 31 DEFs with none empty, 141 epic-parented LLDs needing none, 0 of 21 ISSUEs carrying a story list.
findings.action: Treat as primary-source evidence the review engine structurally cannot reach, exactly as on the previous ISSUE's equivalent claim. A reviewer wanting to check it must re-enumerate .insrc/artifacts; the probes cannot, since they grep src only.

findings.premise: This defect shares its root PATTERN with the folder-fork ISSUE already on the ledger (ISSUE-e20235c17f083a16): in both, a downstream stage synthesises a property it should inherit from the work item's definition artifact, which is why the fix intent asks for the two to be designed as one rule.
findings.evidence: Confirmed, and worth stating because it is the premise the user's 'design both together' instruction rests on. The DEF-only upstream read the folder-fork ISSUE diagnoses resolves at storage.ts:241, `readArtifactCore(repoPath, defineArtifactId(epicHash))`, with exactly one non-test hit. The `epicSlug ?? epicHash` degradation pattern returns 18 non-test source hits across gates.ts, the two build-step phases and storage.ts, consistent with the 7 inside storage.ts counted earlier plus further sites elsewhere. Both defects are therefore instances of one pattern: a downstream stage supplying for itself what the definition artifact should have supplied.
findings.action: none - the shared root pattern is real, which is what makes a single design legitimate rather than a convenient framing

body.title: Standalone and bugfix Stories get no acceptance criteria, so the design document ends up writing the contract it is judged against
body.reproduction: Run any standalone or bugfix work item through the design stage and look at the Story handed to it. The acceptance criteria list is empty every time, and so is the constraints list, so the design document authors its own criteria and the later stages then check it against those. Observed across the whole artifact store rather than on one example: of 55 standalone design documents, 55 supplied their own criteria. For comparison the epic-parented route never does this: 163 stories across 31 definition artifacts all carry criteria, and none of the 141 epic-parented design documents had to invent any. None of the 21 issue records carries a story list at all. The effect is easy to miss because nothing errors. The design document's own audit asks whether every acceptance criterion has a proving test, and with an empty criteria list that check passes every time while proving nothing, so a reader sees a green audit rather than a missing contract.
body.rootCause: The function that builds the Story for a standalone or bugfix run returns a stub rather than reading anything. In src/workflow/runners/design-story/standalone.ts, standaloneStoryContext takes only the triage parameters and the run's focus text, and at line 57 it sets acceptanceCriteria to an empty array, then at line 71 it returns an empty constraints array alongside. The module's import list is types only, so it has no capability to read an artifact even in principle: it cannot consult the approved issue record or a brainstorm spec, because it never opens the artifact store. Both of the values a later stage would want are therefore absent by construction rather than by a lookup that failed. The raw material exists and is discarded. An issue record's body carries a title, a reproduction, a root cause and a fix intent, and on a live record those measure 117, 1320, 3034 and 1008 characters respectively, with the fix intent being exactly the statement acceptance criteria should be derived from. The two call sites that consume this context, orchestrator.ts:1916-1917 for the design context slice and runners/design-story/index.ts:93-94 for the whole context, both receive the stub unchanged. A secondary symptom from the same stub: the Story's title and its user-value field both default to the same focus string, so they come out identical verbatim. This is the same shape of defect as the folder-fork issue already on the ledger, where a later stage recomputed a property instead of inheriting it from the work item's definition artifact; here the later stage invents a contract instead of inheriting one.
body.fixIntent: A standalone or bugfix Story should arrive at design with an acceptance contract it did not write. The criteria and constraints a design document is judged against must originate outside that document, so that the later stages are checking work against an independent statement of what done means rather than against the design's own claims. Whatever the source, the empty-by-construction stub should go, and an empty criteria list should stop being something the pipeline can produce silently and pass an audit with. The design stage must settle several questions this record deliberately leaves open: whether the criteria are authored into the issue record at the issue stage, derived from the fix intent that record already carries, elicited from the user, or ratified at an approval gate; whether that requires the issue record's stored shape to carry them, which would affect the 21 records already on disk; what should happen to the 55 existing standalone design documents whose criteria are self-authored; and whether an empty criteria list should become a hard failure at the design gate rather than a silent pass. It should also be designed alongside the folder-fork issue already on the ledger, so the two express one rule about inheriting from the definition artifact rather than two separate patches.
